label: QuickJS-ng (rquickjs)
notes: A session builds the whole engine (nothing shared between sessions), applies its limits, registers the host call function, then evaluates 1 + 1 and reads 2 back in Rust. Limits: Runtime::set_memory_limit(64MiB), set_max_stack_size(1MiB), set_interrupt_handler (returns false); Context::full has no I/O modules.
Memory: resident growth across 1,000 live sessions (stopped by target), measured first in a fresh process.

Tool call: the guest calls a registered Rust function on its own stack. Median of per-batch means, 1,000,000 calls in batches of 1,000 after 100,000 warm-ups; mean 0.7611 µs, slowest batch 1.4158 µs per call; 0.7604 µs of CPU per call.
Native QuickJS: rquickjs-sys 0.14.0 bundles quickjs-ng 0.16.2 (not Bellard QuickJS), compiled by cc with the crate's default flags; a native comparison point for QuickJS compiled to Wasm.
Session = new Runtime (own GC heap and memory limit) + Context::full + global call; runtimes are not shared across sessions.
Host fn is Function::new(ctx, fn(Ctx, Object) -> Result<Object>); reading args.s copies it into a Rust String to take its length (rquickjs exposes no borrowed length), about 22 bytes per call.
Compute: not measured in the Rust host.
